title.en: Free Trade Agreement (FTA) vs Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA)
title.hi: Free Trade Agreement (FTA) vs Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA)

rows.en: Covers a broad range of goods and services with zero or reduced tariffs.
rows.hi: Covers a broad range of goods and services with zero or reduced tariffs.

rows.en: Covers a limited list of goods with reduced tariffs.
rows.hi: Covers a limited list of goods with reduced tariffs.

rows.en: Aims for near-zero tariffs on most traded items.
rows.hi: Aims for near-zero tariffs on most traded items.

rows.en: Provides preferential access but not necessarily zero tariffs.
rows.hi: Provides preferential access but not necessarily zero tariffs.

rows.en: Both aim to enhance bilateral or regional trade by reducing trade barriers.
rows.hi: Both aim to enhance bilateral or regional trade by reducing trade barriers.

rows.en: Both must generally adhere to WTO rules, specifically the Enabling Clause or Article XXIV of GATT.
rows.hi: Both must generally adhere to WTO rules, specifically the Enabling Clause or Article XXIV of GATT.

clarification.en: An FTA allows members to set their own external tariffs, whereas a Customs Union requires members to adopt a common external tariff.
clarification.hi: An FTA allows members to set their own external tariffs, whereas a Customs Union requires members to adopt a common external tariff.

relationship.en: Trade agreements influence export-import volumes, directly impacting the current account balance.
relationship.hi: Trade agreements influence export-import volumes, directly impacting the current account balance.
